messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: geo-dns-resolver-error spike in eu-west-1. 60% of DNS queries returning SERVFAIL from our resolver probes. Customers reporting 502/504 across EU regions. Paging oncall.
Elaine: Got it, I'm oncall. Looking at dashboard now — latency and error rate spike aligns with DNS probe failures.
Elaine: Quick checks: curl to primary eu loadbalancer shows 200 from inside cluster, but external synthetic checks show 502. Suspect DNS resolution intermittency at the resolver/edge layer.
Kai: I'm pulling provider metrics. Cloudflare resolver pool in EU region showing elevated 5xx on their public resolver. Route53 health checks look OK for origin. Could be resolver cache poisoning/eviction or propagation lag on weighted failover entries.
Jun: Can you paste the dig from our monitoring runner?
Elaine: paste: ```
; dig +short @1.1.1.1 app.redwood-inference.eu A
SERVFAIL
; dig +short @8.8.8.8 app.redwood-inference.eu A
93.184.216.34
```
Kai: So some resolvers return answer, others SERVFAIL. That's classic noisy resolver cache or upstream rate limiting. Also seeing sudden increase in queries per second to our geoDNS records from a few ASN ranges.
Maria: Customer impact: Support ticket stream shows 23 customers affected (mostly EU SaaS customers) with increased error rates and slow page loads. Some are sending retries; a few saw session drops.
Elaine: Triage plan: 1) Short-term failover: update geodns to route traffic away from EU resolver-backed pool to eu-fallback (lower weight to primary, increase fallback). 2) Reduce TTL on geo records to 20s to speed propagation for our change. 3) Open tickets with Cloudflare + AWS (Route53) with probe data. 4) Monitor for rollback.
Sam: Agreed. Make the change and I'll monitor from external vantage points. Post the exact change you plan.
Elaine: Doing it via internal geodns UI. Change set: set weight eu-primary -> 10, eu-fallback -> 90; set TTL 300 -> 20. Command shown for infra audit (terraform plan will be attached to incident): ```
# pseudo change shown for audit
resource "redwood_geodns_record" "app" {
  name = "app.redwood-inference.eu"
  ttl  = 20
  records = ["eu-primary.example.net","eu-fallback.example.net"]
  weights = [10,90]
}
```
Jun: Applying now. Will run validation dig loop from 5 external resolvers.
Jun: validation logs: ```
[05:01:12] -> 1.1.1.1 -> 93.184.216.34
[05:01:15] -> 8.8.8.8 -> 93.184.216.34
[05:01:20] -> 185.60.112.XX -> SERVFAIL
[05:01:25] -> 2a00:1450:XXXX -> 93.184.216.34
```
Kai: After weight shift, external resolvers increasingly get the eu-fallback IPs. Still seeing some SERVFAIL from specific ASNs but overall client-side 5xx rate down ~60%.
Maria: Notifying affected customers: I've posted a short status update to status.redwood.com and added a note to affected support tickets referencing the mitigation and ETA.
Elaine: Opening vendor tickets now. Cloudflare support ticket #CF-20456: noisy resolver cache / upstream rate limit suspected. AWS ticket #R53-7781: confirm that Route53 is serving our weight changes and propagation behavior. Attaching probe logs.
Sam: Good. Keep TTL low for now. Once stable for 30m, we can slowly restore weights and increase TTL back to 300s. Also, add a monitoring alert for resolver-level SERVFAIL ratio so this doesn't burn cycles next time.
Elaine: Agree. Added alert rule with 5% SERVFAIL threshold in probing service.
Jun: FYI observed one edge case: an internal healthcheck IP for eu-primary still shows healthy from origin but fails DNS at some resolvers — that suggests external resolver layer issue rather than origin.
Kai: Preparing packet captures and resolver logs to include in Cloudflare ticket. Also checking whether our EDNS options trigger any filter.
Maria: Updating status page to indicate mitigation in place. Customers asked about rollback risk; I've added a note we may flip back if degraded.
Elaine: Monitoring: client 5xx rate now down to baseline +10% (was +90%). Continued watch. Oncall handoff planned: Sam will take incident lead in 30m when I sign off to handle a pager rotation.
Sam: Taking lead in 30m. I'll coordinate vendor follow-up and run through post-incident RCA checklist.
Elaine: Thanks team. Incident record created: INC-2402001111. Will attach timeline + commands. Please add any extra logs to the incident doc.
incident-bot: Update: incident status -> mitigation applied (geo-dns failover), severity -> partial-service-degradation, incident_id -> INC-2402001111.
Elaine: handing off to Sam now — leaving a short runbook: if errors rise above 15% re-route traffic permanently to fallback and escalate to Cloudflare Sev2.
Sam: Acknowledged. I'll continue monitoring and update postmortem once stable. :thumbsup:
